title: Out of Boundary Paths
summary: Given an m x n grid and a ball starting at [startRow, startColumn], calculate the number of paths to move the ball out of the grid in at most maxMove moves.
statement: Given an m x n grid and a ball starting at [startRow, startColumn], calculate the number of paths to move the ball out of the grid in at most maxMove moves. Return the count modulo 10^9 + 7.
constraints: Start inside an m by n grid and move one cell in four directions.
Count paths that leave the grid in at most maxMove moves, modulo 1000000007.
Paths stop when they first leave.
hints: The state is row, column, and moves remaining.
Leaving contributes one immediately; staying inside with no moves contributes zero.
Memoize the sum of four next states modulo the limit.
Each move sequence has a unique first step and is counted exactly when it first crosses the grid edge.
editorial: Each move sequence has a unique first step and is counted exactly when it first crosses the grid edge.

tests.explanation: Six move sequences leave the two-by-two grid within two moves.
Twelve paths leave the one-row grid within three moves.
